description: The Fire Rooster in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1957 and 2017 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Rooster is the Rooster born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the tenth animal. It combines the Rooster's precision with Fire's qualities. Fire Rooster years between 1924 and 2044 are 1957 and 2017. The Rooster's fixed element is Metal.

sections.heading: The Fire Rooster personality
paragraphs: Fire controls Metal, and a Rooster always carries Metal, so a Fire stem is said to heat this exacting animal from outside, testing and tempering its resolve. The traditional result is a vivid, forceful personality: confident, outspoken, hard-driving and keen to be recognised for excellent work. Fire Roosters are portrayed as organised leaders with plenty of flair, happy to take charge and set the pace. They tend to be loyal and honest to a fault. Under that heat, though, the Rooster's candour can become bluntness, and readings point to a quick temper, a need for admiration and a tendency to dig in when their judgement is questioned in public. Few people work harder to earn the praise they want.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: Fire Rooster at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

The Fire Rooster loves to be seen doing excellent work. Broadcasting, fashion, management, event direction and public speaking suit it, since confidence and precision both shine there. It sets high standards for itself and others and tends to take charge naturally, especially when a project is visibly floundering. Recognition, an audience and a well-polished result are its favourite rewards. In love, the Fire Rooster is passionate, proud and protective, keen to show off a partner as much as itself. It needs admiration and loyalty. Friction comes from bluntness and pride: it may criticise sharply in the heat of the moment and then find an apology unusually difficult to deliver.

sections.heading: Fire Rooster years and dates
paragraphs: Fire Rooster years in the Lunar New Year table run from January 31, 1957 to February 17, 1958 and from January 28, 2017 to February 15, 2018. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1957 anyone born before Jan 31 is a Fire Monkey, not a Fire Rooster. Sixty years separate each Fire Rooster year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Fire Rooster year is Yin, matching the Rooster's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Ding-You: Ding is the yin Fire stem and You is the Rooster's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Monkey year (before January 31, 1957) and the Fire Monkey year (before January 28, 2017), and births in the weeks after each Fire Rooster year ends belong to the Earth Dog. The new year itself fell on a Thursday in 1957 and Saturday in 2017.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Rooster
paragraphs: The Fire Rooster tends to grow by learning that being right and being heard are not the same thing. Delivering critique privately, and pairing it with something genuinely appreciated, makes their honesty far more effective. A short pause before reacting to perceived slights also helps. Because they push themselves hard, regular rest protects against the irritability that comes with exhaustion. Fire Roosters often shine in leadership, performance and project management, where their energy and standards are assets. Letting others take the stage sometimes builds loyalty. Tempered in this way, their brilliance warms rather than scorches.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Rooster shares the Rooster's San He trine with the Ox and Snake (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Dragon, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rabbit. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Rooster years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1957 (from January 31, 1957) and 2017 (from January 28, 2017). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Rooster's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Rooster's fixed element is Metal; in the five-element cycles fire controls Metal. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Rooster?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox and Snake (San He) and the Dragon (Liu He). The Rabbit is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Rooster called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ding-You. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Ding, followed by its earthly branch, here You for the Rooster, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Rooster different from other Roosters?
faq.answer: All Roosters share precision, candour and diligence. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
